name: C++ Actor Framework
listed_description: An Open Source Implementation of the Actor Model in C++.
reason: No numbers reachable. README, repo docs (doc/pdf holds only design diagrams) and the actor-framework/benchmarks repo README (microbenchmark suite, no results, no licence shown) carry no figures. Real baselines would be Erlang, Akka, Charm++ and other actor runtimes, not libevent or standard async I/O, and the category is actor and concurrency runtime rather than event-loops-io. Lead: Charousset, Hiesgen, Schmidt 'Revisiting Actor Programming in C++' (Computer Languages, Systems & Structures 2016, arXiv 1505.07368); a WebSearch snippet of its abstract says CAF outperforms Erlang, Charm++, SalsaLite, Scala, ActorFoundry and OpenMPI up to 64 cores at low memory, but the paper itself (arxiv.org, ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org, reposit.haw-hamburg.de, inet.haw-hamburg.de, hgpu.org) is EGRESS_BLOCKED here so no number could be read. Worth a retry from a session with paper access; would be a B record on the CAF benchmarks repo plus the paper.

name: C++ REST SDK
reason: No claim of being faster and no numbers in the repo (archived 2026-06-01; README now recommends libcurl or Boost.Beast). The only numeric comparison found is the independent shootout https://github.com/guteksan/REST-CPP-benchmark (issue #1432), where cpprestsdk v2.10.15 is the slowest or ties: 3.401 s against Crow 1.536 s, Pistache 1.059 s, Restbed 1.333 s, Restinio 1.025 s, cpp-httplib 3.015 s (10,000 POSTs, t=0 ms, local, 28 threads), and it deadlocks when service threads are fewer than client producers.

name: C++ wfrest
reason: README only says 'Fast, efficient' with no numbers. benchmark/ holds wfrest and libhv echo servers plus wrk commands but no results. docs/benchmark_results.md compares wfrest's own CachedFile serving with its own normal static serving (2.0x to 3.8x, wrk) which is a self comparison, not a named external baseline. docs/static_file_optimization.md cites issue #272 that default static file serving is up to 4 times slower than a regular Apache setup for small files, i.e. evidence against being faster. Sogou Workflow (the engine underneath) publishes its own nginx comparisons but that is a different project.

name: c-ares
listed_description: A C library for asynchronous DNS requests.
reason: No benchmark in README, RELEASE-NOTES.md, docs or test/ (no benchmark files; ares_queryloop.c is a query-loop tool). The only numbers found are against it: issue #500 'Under load, ares_getaddrinfo is 3x slower than libc getaddrinfo (w/ threadpool)', 50 simultaneous lookups on an Apple M1 Max under bun 0.4.1: libc 749.81 ms/iter, c-ares 2.38 s/iter, macOS getaddrinfo_async 176.99 ms/iter (reporter found two small socket writes per call for AF_UNSPEC; closed Jan 2023, resolution not visible). The directional claim that c-ares is faster than getaddrinfo in Node.js docs has no numbers; c-ares.org mailing list archives with 2007 timings were EGRESS_BLOCKED.

name: CHL
listed_description: C Hypertext Library - A library for writing web applications in C.
reason: README, repo page and file list contain no benchmark or performance numbers and no comparison with any server or library; it is a CGI and FastCGI helper library (licence shown LGPL-3.0 on the repo page, tagged GPL-3.0-only in the list).

name: Civetweb
listed_description: Provides easy to use, powerful, C/C++ embeddable web server with optional CGI, SSL and Lua support.
reason: No benchmark or speed comparison in README, docs/ (UserManual, Embedding and others mention performance only in config advice), or issues (searches for benchmark and nginx returned nothing; performance issues #1309, #1163, #887 are not comparisons). Four WebSearch queries for independent shootouts including civetweb found none with numbers.
